note: Derived from example-k8s .github/workflows/validate.yml. Every check here is expressible as trusted-tool-over-untrusted-data AND passes on example-k8s main -- a check list that cannot pass on the base is not a gate, it is an outage. Two validate.yml steps are DELIBERATELY absent, and the omission is a stated boundary rather than an oversight: (1) the kustomize render (`kustomize build base/ledger examples/overlays/* deploy admin`) -- kustomize reads kustomization.yaml FROM the tree, which is untrusted content controlling execution and resource resolution, exactly what the trusted-tool-over-untrusted-data rule forbids; without the render, kubeconform over deploy/ is a category error (it holds pre-substitution ${VAR} templates, not manifests), so deploy/ manifests are NOT schema-validated here and deploy/ is covered only by the grep-shaped guards below. (2) shellcheck -- it takes an explicit file list from `git ls-files '*.sh'`, which this runner's fixed-argv model cannot express.

checks.name: ck-bash-default-expansion
checks.note: validate.yml step 'Forbid bash-default expansions in ConfigMap-shipped scripts'. Flux's envsubst evaluates ${VAR:-x}/${VAR:=x} in ConfigMap-shipped scripts, silently applying a default in-cluster (example-k8s docs/usage.md sharp edge 4). This is the fail-open class that motivated the whole tool.

checks.name: ck-secret-denylist
checks.note: validate.yml step 'Secret / denylist scan', first pattern. No SOPS material and no private-deployment hostnames/namespaces/paths may land in this PUBLIC repo. The bracketed character classes keep the pattern from matching its own text.

checks.name: ck-credential-shaped
checks.note: validate.yml step 'Secret / denylist scan', second pattern: the generic article rather than the six enumerated strings -- a real JWT, a PEM private key, a GitHub token, an AWS access-key id. An advisory fix is exactly the kind of hurried change that carries one in.

checks.name: kubeconform-base
checks.note: validate.yml's kubeconform step, restricted to the trees that validate WITHOUT the kustomize render. `Valid: [1-9]` is the positive-work assertion: kubeconform exits 0 over a directory holding no manifests, so a bare zero exit would certify an emptied base/.

checks.name: kubeconform-admin
checks.note: Same, over admin/. Measured on example-k8s main: 5 resources in 2 files, Valid: 4.
